question: Arrange the fractions frac{5}9, frac{4}7, frac{3}5 and, frac{2}3 in ascending order.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the fractions into percentages to easily compare their values.

5/9 ≈ 55.55%, 4/7 ≈ 57.14%, 3/5 = 60%, 2/3 ≈ 66.67%

Arranging the percentages in ascending order: 55.55% [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fractions to arrange: 5/9, 4/7, 3/5, 2/3

**Method Used:**

LCM Equalization Method

 Comparing Fractions (Percentage Value) 5/9 55.55% 4/7 57.14% 3/5 60.00% 2/3 66.67% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM of denominators (9, 7, 5, 3) = 9 × 7 × 5 = 315

⇒ Convert each fraction so that the denominator becomes 315:

⇒ 5/9 = (5 × 35) ÷ (9 × 35) = 175/315

⇒ 4/7 = (4 × 45) ÷ (7 × 45) = 180/315

⇒ 3/5 = (3 × 63) ÷ (5 × 63) = 189/315

⇒ 2/3 = (2 × 105) ÷ (3 × 105) = 210/315

⇒ Comparing the numerators: 175 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Method

To compare two fractions a/b and c/d, cross-multiply to get a×d and b×c. If a×d < b×c, then the first fraction is smaller (a/b < c/d).

Decimal Conversion Method

Convert each fraction to its decimal equivalent by simply dividing the numerator by the denominator. Compare the resulting decimal numbers up to 2 to 3 decimal places for accurate results.

Difference Method

When the difference between the numerator and denominator is the exact same for a set of proper fractions, the fraction with the largest numerator is strictly the greatest.
